- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap next 3-day forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–3% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment spikes in early forecast window (days 1–5); apply 10% downward bias to first 5 forecast days if sentiment >0.6.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price drops after 2–3 consecutive peaks), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead by -2% to -5% to align with observed reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting to reduce false peaks.
